title: Internal group-algebra actions and exactness of the forgetful functor
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring on a small coherent site of profinite sets with finite jointly surjective coverings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention]. Work in internal $A$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], with internal relative tensor [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]. Write $A[X]$ for the free internal module on a condensed set $X$, with its canonical generalized generators $[x]$, as in [def-sfb-condensed-free-module-adjunction]. Let $G$ be a profinite group and $\underline G(S)=C(S,G)$ its condensed group. Let $\mathcal A_G(A)$ be the category of natural $A(S)$-linear $C(S,G)$-actions on section modules and equivariant internal-module maps [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. The internal module $B=A[\underline G]$ has a monoid-object structure in internal $A$-modules, with multiplication and unit
$$[g]\otimes[h]\longmapsto[gh],\qquad 1\longmapsto[1].$$
It need not be commutative. There is an equivalence
$$\mathcal A_G(A)\simeq\operatorname{Mod}_B(\operatorname{Mod}_A),$$
where the right side means module objects for this monoid [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and the equivalence commutes with forgetting to internal $A$-modules. It sends the sectionwise action $gm$ to the unique internal $B$-action extending $[g]\otimes m\mapsto gm$; conversely it restricts a $B$-action to the canonical generators. More precisely, for every profinite $S$, the natural bilinear map
$$A(S)[C(S,G)]\times M(S)\longrightarrow M(S),\qquad (\sum a_g[g],m)\longmapsto\sum a_g(gm)$$
extends uniquely through module sheafification to the bilinear sheaf action, hence to $B\otimes_A M\to M$. This characterization does not require global finite-generator expressions for sections of $B$.
The category $\mathcal A_G(A)$ is abelian. Its forgetful functor creates kernels, cokernels and images, with uniquely induced actions on the underlying subobjects and quotients. An equivariant complex is exact, including epimorphic augmentation, if and only if its underlying internal-module complex is exact.
For a condensed set $X$ with an internal $\underline G$-action, linearization gives the action $[g]\otimes[x]\mapsto[gx]$ on $A[X]$. An equivariant map $u:X\to Y$ induces an equivariant $A[u]$, and equivariance of a map from $A[X]$ is detected on generalized generators. If an internal module $T$ has trivial action, tensoring an equivariant module with $T$ gives the natural action $g(m\otimes t)=(gm)\otimes t$; equivariant maps tensor to equivariant maps and the resulting tensor functor is additive.

proof.text: Put $K=\underline G$. It is a sheaf of groups by [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure]. Apply [lem-sfb-condensed-free-linearization-tensor] to $K\times K\to K$ and $1\to K$: the composites $B\otimes_A B\cong A[K\times K]\to A[K]=B$ and $A\cong A[1]\to B$ define multiplication and unit. Their formulas are $[g]\otimes[h]\mapsto[gh]$ and $1\mapsto[1]$. Under the cited associator and unitor comparisons, the two associativity maps send $[g]\otimes[h]\otimes[k]$ respectively to $[(gh)k]$ and $[g(hk)]$; these agree by the group law. The unit maps similarly send $[g]$ to $[1g]=[g]=[g1]$. Detection on generators in the same lemma proves the monoid laws. No commutativity of $G$ was used.

source.place: Paragraph (3), internal group-algebra construction; agent expansion of the extracted bar input

proof.text: Let $M$ have the natural sectionwise action in [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Write $F_K(S)=A(S)[K(S)]$. Define $b_S(\sum a_g[g],m)=\sum a_g(gm)$. This is $A(S)$-bilinear because each $g$ acts linearly; restriction compatibility follows from the naturality of the given action. By [lem-sfb-condensed-free-linearization-tensor], $F_K^\#=E_A(B)$. Apply [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension] with $\mathcal O=A$, $\mathcal F=F_K$, and $\mathcal G=\mathcal H=E_A(M)$ (the latter already sheaves). It extends $b$ uniquely to a bilinear sheaf map $E_A(B)\times E_A(M)\to E_A(M)$. The tensor universal property [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] and the pure-tensor comparison [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] therefore give a unique internal map $\gamma:B\otimes_A M\to M$ with $\gamma([g]\otimes m)=gm$. This is an extension from the free presheaf, not a claim that every section of $B$ is a finite sum of global generators.

source.place: Tag 0GMW (lemma-sheafification-tensor), bilinear extension and tensor universal property in Section 03EK; application to the internal action

proof.text: Use $B\otimes_A B\cong A[K\times K]$ from [lem-sfb-condensed-free-linearization-tensor] to identify the source of the two module-associativity maps with $A[K\times K]\otimes_A M$, via associators. On the free presheaf $F_{K\times K}(S)$ paired with $E_A(M)(S)$, both maps send $[(g,h)],m$ to $(gh)m=g(hm)$. Linearity then gives equality for every finite sum $\sum c_{g,h}[(g,h)]$. Uniqueness in [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension], applied to $F_{K\times K}$ and $E_A(M)$, proves equality of the two associated bilinear sheaf maps; the injectivity of the bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_A(\mathcal F\otimes_A\mathcal G,\mathcal H)\cong\mathrm{Bilin}_A(\mathcal F\times\mathcal G,\mathcal H)$ of [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] then gives equality of the two maps on the sheafified tensor. The comparison [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] respects associators, so this is exactly the internal module associativity axiom of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. For the unit, $b([1],m)=m$ on every section; the tensor unit comparison gives the internal unitality axiom. Thus the constructed map is a $B$-module action.

source.place: Paragraph (3), verification of internal group-algebra action laws; agent expansion using the sheafification universal properties

proof.text: Conversely, for an internal $B$-module define $gm=\gamma([g]\otimes m)$. Internal linearity and naturality give $A(S)$-linearity and restriction compatibility. The module laws give $1m=m$ and $(gh)m=g(hm)$; the inverse operator is that of $g^{-1}$. These are the objects of [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Restricting an extended action returns its original values $gm$. Extending a restricted action returns the original $\gamma$ by the bilinear extension uniqueness [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension], the tensor universal property [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] and the tensor comparison [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison]. For a map $f:M\to N$, $B$-linearity implies $f(gm)=gf(m)$. Conversely this equation implies $f(\sum a_g gm)=\sum a_g gf(m)$, hence commutation with the entire extended action by the same uniqueness and the tensor universal property [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal]. Thus both constructions act as the identity on underlying maps and give inverse functors, with identity unit and counit; they commute with forgetting to internal $A$-modules.

source.place: Paragraph (3), inverse equivalence and its compatibility with the underlying internal module; agent argument

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure] with $R=A$, $J=G$: its hypotheses are exactly the fixed small coherent site, coefficient universe and commutative condensed ring here. It gives an abelian action category and states that forgetting action creates sectionwise kernels and sheafified sectionwise cokernels and detects exactness. In particular it supplies the required kernel and cokernel actions. They are uniquely determined by equivariance of the structure maps: the kernel inclusion is a monomorphism, so it determines the restricted action; the cokernel projection is an epimorphism of sheaves, so two actions agreeing after it agree after every local lift, hence agree. The latter assertion is sheaf-local, not surjectivity on sections.

source.place: Paragraph (3), existing action-category infrastructure, abelianness and creation of kernels and cokernels

proof.text: For an equivariant $f$, take the kernel of its equivariant cokernel; by step 5 its underlying subobject is $\ker(\operatorname{coker}(Uf))=\operatorname{im}(Uf)$, with its unique induced action. This is the image of $f$ in the abelian action category. The exactness detection of [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure] therefore identifies the equality of image and kernel in each degree with the same equality after forgetting. An augmentation is epimorphic exactly when its cokernel is zero; creation of cokernels and detection of zero objects in the same cited statement prove this equivalence as well. These statements concern internal-module exactness, not sectionwise surjectivity.

source.place: Paragraph (3), images and augmented exact complexes; elementary kernel-cokernel argument from the cited infrastructure

proof.text: For a condensed $G$-set $X$, give $F_X(S)=A(S)[X(S)]$ the action $g(\sum a_x[x])=\sum a_x[gx]$. It is natural, linear and satisfies $1[x]=[x]$ and $g(h[x])=[(gh)x]$. The sheafification reflector [lem-sfb-equivariant-module-sheafification-reflector] gives its unique action on $F_X^\#$, which is $E_A(A[X])$ by [lem-sfb-condensed-free-linearization-tensor]. Step 2 translates this to $[g]\otimes[x]\mapsto[gx]$. If $u$ is equivariant then $A[u](g[x])=[u(gx)]=[gu(x)]=gA[u]([x])$; the reflector makes $A[u]$ equivariant after sheafification. For $f:A[X]\to M$, the equivariance equation is equality of maps $A[K]\otimes_A A[X]\cong A[K\times X]\to M$. Generator detection in the free-linearization lemma says it is equivalent to $f([gx])=g f([x])$ for all generalized $g,x$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), linearization of actions and detection of equivariance on generalized generators; agent expansion

proof.text: Let $T$ have trivial action. On the presheaf $P(S)=E_A(M)(S)\otimes_{A(S)}E_A(T)(S)$ define $g(m\otimes t)=(gm)\otimes t$. Balancedness follows from $g(am)=a(gm)$; restriction naturality and the group laws follow on pure tensors, which generate each presheaf tensor module. Apply [lem-sfb-equivariant-module-sheafification-reflector] to obtain the action on $P^\#$. By [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] this is the required underlying internal tensor $M\otimes_A T$. If $f$ is equivariant, $f\otimes1$ commutes with $g$ on each presheaf pure tensor, so its sheafification is equivariant by the reflector. Finally $((f+f')\otimes1)(m\otimes t)=f(m)\otimes t+f'(m)\otimes t$ and $(0\otimes1)(m\otimes t)=0$. The bilinear universal property [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] extends these equalities to tensor sheaves. Thus the resulting functor is additive. The identical calculation with an equivariant map in the trivially acted-on factor proves the two-variable map assertion.
